courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Subject Curriculum and Teaching (Major: Chinese Language)
courses.description:
This course is designed to equip the students with essential techniques and knowledge in the teaching of Chinese Language. It will focus on the following topics: (1) objectives of Chinese Language teaching; (2) preparation of teaching material; (3) lesson planning; (4) teaching tools; (5) teaching methods; (6) evaluation; and (7) extra-curricular activities.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
認識現行課程的基本理念、發展方向、課程宗旨、學習目標及學習範疇之內涵；
認識主要的教學理論、教學方法、教學活動及教學資源等；
具備設計單元教學活動的能力；
具備實踐有效教學活動的能力；
能善用教學資源來優化教學效果。

中文科課程改革檢視；
單元教學；
教學設計；
教學方法；
語文能力綜合訓練；
各體文教學；
教材編選及教學媒體的應用；
微格教學及分析。

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Subject Curriculum and Teaching (Major: English)
courses.description:
This course seeks to equip teachers of English Language with the skills necessary for future self-development in the face of changing theories of language and language teaching/learning by offering a foundation in both areas, together with practical experience of classroom teaching, action research, self evaluation and the design, implementation and evaluation of the language curriculum. The following topics are also covered: (1) the teaching of grammar, listening, speaking, reading and writing; (2) preparing students for public examinations; (3) student motivation, cooperative learning and the roles of spoken and written discourse in the language learning process; (4) planning the language learning process and units within it; and (5) the needs of remedial and ‘mixed ability’ language learners.

Note: The assessment criteria refer to:
(a) Knowledge of theory and pedagogy,
(b) Competence in applying pedagogical knowledge in classroom teaching,
(c) Concern for personal professional development

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.course_syllabus:
• An overview of second language teaching methodology

• The official Hong Kong English Language curriculum

• Planning for teaching: Schemes of work, Unit Plans, Lesson Plans

• Teaching grammar

• Teaching vocabulary

• Developing students’ competence in the four skills

• Managing a language lesson

• Materials design and adaptation

• Assessment

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Subject Curriculum and Teaching (Major: Chinese History)
courses.description:
This course will first examine the value of learning history and then go on to discuss the objectives of teaching the subject in secondary schools. It will also explore areas including: (1) the suitability of the existing curriculum and curriculum design; (2) effective teaching methods; (3) the use of teaching aids; (4) the planning of backing activities; and (5) examination and evaluation methods. The course consists of lecture seminars, excursions and simulated teaching sessions. Emphasis will be put on assisting students in developing practical and feasible solutions to meet educational objectives.

courses.description:
This course aims at helping teachers to understand more deeply the trends of geographical education and different kinds of curriculum design in geography, to learn how to adopt a student-centred approach and to use appropriate teaching strategies. The course content includes: (1) trends in geography and geographical education; (2) the junior and senior secondary curricula in Hong Kong; (3) teaching strategies in- and out-of-the-classroom; (4) use of teaching aids and other teaching materials; and (5) methods of student evaluation.

To examine the development and implementation of biology curricula in Hong Kong as well as in overseas countries (e.g. BSCS in the U.S. and the Nuffield Biology project in the U.K.); to formulate instructional goals and objectives for secondary school biology educational; and to devise instructional plans to achieve such goals. courses.title: Subject Curriculum and Teaching (Major: Visual Arts)
courses.description:
This course aims at equipping students with the necessary knowledge and skills to be a qualified visual arts teacher or even a panel head in secondary school. As a qualified visual arts teacher, they should be familiar with the present visual arts curriculum and hence they can tailor-make and provide school-based curriculum to different students.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
• To appreciate and comprehend the cultural significance of the arts and its concrete idea of the nature, meaning and function of art education.
• To give brief idea of the visual arts curriculum and its development in secondary school.
• To apply the concepts and rationale of art education theories for developing visual arts curriculum (creation and appreciation) for secondary students.
• To select, design, develop and evaluate different types of activities and materials in planning and tailor-making a visual arts lesson – planning, implementing and evaluation.
• To explain and comprehend childhood developmental stages and their relationship to art-making.
• To become acquainted with different pedagogical theories of visual arts in developing Hong Kong visual arts curriculum and teaching in secondary school.
• To apply the concepts and rationale in developing formal and informal art education curriculum in secondary school.
• To use multimedia technology to enhance secondary students’ learning experience during visual arts lesson.
• To reflect concepts and critical theories relating to the development of visual arts education and visual culture.
• To identify the trend and development of art education in the globe.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. The nature of art education: a broad perspective on the visual arts and related aesthetic / art critical concepts and their application in a secondary school context
2. Comparative study on the curriculum and development of visual arts education in Hong Kong
3. Curriculum integration: studio practice / art appreciation / art criticism (art history and aesthetics)
4. Curriculum Design in visual arts: planning. implementing and evaluation
5. Childhood developmental stages and their relationship to art-making
6. Theories on pedagogy of visual arts
7. Formal and non-formal curriculum in secondary school
8. Application of I. T. and multi-media and case study
9. Visual arts and creative education and its relationship with visual culture
10. Trends in art education

courses.description:
This course introduces students to principles, concepts and techniques of teaching Business, Accounting and Financial Studies (BAFS) at secondary schools. It aims at enabling students to integrate knowledge of teaching methodology and skills in practical teaching, subject curriculum and assessment. Through taking part in various learning tasks and classroom discussions and engaging in critical reflection, students will be encouraged to develop their personal theory of teaching.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should be able to:

• Acquire knowledge and skills necessary for Business (BAFS) teaching, subject curriculum and assessment;
• Apply their knowledge and skills in lesson plan and material design as well as classroom teaching for facilitating the teaching and learning of BAFS

• critically evaluate instructional strategies, pedagogical skills and learning processes in BAFS by applying the concepts and principles learnt; and

develop their personal theory and skills of Business teaching
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Teaching Business subjects (BAFS) at secondary schools: Factors affecting learning Business subjects (BAFS); BAFS teaching approaches and methods; BAFS curriculum; Business subject (BAFS) education reforms in Hong Kong

2. Teaching of the pedagogical components in Business, Accounting and Financial Studies (BAFS): Nature of accounting calculation, business analysis and financial application; teaching these skills in the classroom

3. Planning, implementing and evaluating lessons: How to plan, implement and evaluate a BAFS lesson; classroom communication and interaction

4. Assessment and evaluation: Key issues in Business Subject (BAFS) assessment and evaluation; assessment for learning; feedback in learning

courses.description:
This course seeks to equip teachers of English Language with the skills necessary for future self-development in the face of changing theories of language and language
teaching/learning by offering a foundation in both areas, together with practical experience of classroom teaching, action research, self evaluation and the design, implementation and evaluation of the language curriculum. courses.subject: PGDE

courses.description:
To examine the development and implementation of biology curricula in Hong Kong as well as in overseas countries (e.g. BSCS in the U.S. and the Nuffield Biology project in the U.K.); to formulate instructional goals and objectives for secondary school biology educational; and to devise instructional plans to achieve such goals. These plans include the use of classroom, lectures, laboratory experiments and outdoor field-trips. Contents include: (1) role of Biology in secondary education and its relationship with science education; (2) development and treatment of the biology curriculum; and (3) treatment of special topics in biology education.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, participants should be able to :
• have an understanding of the aims, contents, organization and assessment of the Biology curricula in Hong Kong
• develop a sophisticated understanding of important biology concepts, their pedagogical content knowledge and potential alternative conceptions
• understand and enact effective teaching strategies for biology learning
• design and implement effective biological investigations to develop inquiry skills and understanding of nature of science among their students
• understand the nature of science and its importance in science teaching, and infuse it effectively into teaching
• design and implement biology teaching using the science-technology-society-environment (STSE) approach
• be sensitive to the ethical issues around some biological topics and make use of them to foster affective outcomes amongst students
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Reflection on the teaching career and what is good teaching/education
2. Presentation skills for teaching - principles of multimedia teaching and graphic representation
3. Microteaching 1 - each giving a 5-10 minute lecture with slides
4. Classroom questioning and interaction
5. Discipline control
6. Learning progression: organization of topics within/across lessons
7. Planning a lesson and writing lesson plans
8. Misconception and constructivism
9. Misconception in secondary biology
10. Identifying misconceptions (e.g. osmosis) - graphic organizer, concept cartoon
11. Constructivist teaching e.g. 5E teaching model (e.g. osmosis)
12. Hard-to-teach biology concepts - why is it hard and how to deal with it?
13. Microteaching 2 - questioning and interaction to identify misconceptions and construct concepts
14. Group presentation 1 - how to teach a hard-to-teach biology concept
15. Use of tangible models in biology teaching
16. Assessment in biology
17. Setting exam and test papers e.g. HKJSBO, PISA
18. Group presentation 2 - analysis of HKDSE papers and suggested answer
19. Practical work and scientific investigations
20. Microteaching 3 - pre-lab and post-lab talk
21. Teaching about the nature of science in biology
22. Ethical and religious issues in biology teaching
23. Biology curriculum - goals of science education

courses.description:
This course introduces students to principles, concepts and techniques of teaching Business, Accounting and Financial Studies (BAFS) at secondary schools. It aims at enabling students to integrate knowledge of teaching methodology and skills in practical teaching, subject curriculum and assessment. Through taking part in various learning tasks and classroom discussions and engaging in critical reflection, students will be encouraged to develop their personal theory of teaching.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should be able to:

• Acquire knowledge and skills necessary for Business (BAFS) teaching, subject curriculum and assessment;
• Apply their knowledge and skills in lesson plan and material design as well as classroom teaching for facilitating the teaching and learning of BAFS

• critically evaluate instructional strategies, pedagogical skills and learning processes in BAFS by applying the concepts and principles learnt; and

develop their personal theory and skills of Business teaching
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Teaching Business subjects (BAFS) at secondary schools: Factors affecting learning Business subjects (BAFS); BAFS teaching approaches and methods; BAFS curriculum; Business subject (BAFS) education reforms in Hong Kong

2. Teaching of the pedagogical components in Business, Accounting and Financial Studies (BAFS): Nature of accounting calculation, business analysis and financial application; teaching these skills in the classroom

3. Planning, implementing and evaluating lessons: How to plan, implement and evaluate a BAFS lesson; classroom communication and interaction

4. Assessment and evaluation: Key issues in Business Subject (BAFS) assessment and evaluation; assessment for learning; feedback in learning

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Design and Implementation of Student Activities
courses.description:
Contrary to common belief, student activities are not “supplementary” to school curriculum. They comprise an indispensable part of the school curriculum and often a significant part of students’ memories of school life. As the Hong Kong school curriculum reforms, greater significance is focused on extra-curricular, academic, cross-curricular, integrated curricular and life-wide learning activities. Organizing student activities is an integral duty of educators nowadays, and it is a pre-requisite that they know how to design and implement student activities that are both safe and meaningful. This course aims to equip students with knowledge and skills required in design and implementation of student activities. The ultimate goal is to enhance both the processes and outcomes of student activities in the school curriculum and meet educational expectations on student learning through activities. Another aim is to heighten students’ awareness of safety and insurance issues in risk assessment through class activities.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
(1) To understand the educational value of student activities and to illustrate the current status of student activities in secondary school in Hong Kong. (Knowledge)
(2) To master the principles and skills of leading and arranging student activities. (Skills)
(3) Value student activities, and assist students’ growth through student activities. (Attitude)
courses.course_syllabus:
1. The positioning and function of student activities in the school.
2. Planning, organizing and evaluating student activities.
3. Extra-curricular activities (ECA), Life Wide Learning (LWL) and Other Learning Experience (OLE).
4. House, Student Union, Uniform Team, Voluntary Services.
5. Student Activities (including clubs, interest classes and competition) and Large-scale activities (School Picnic, LWL Day, Sports Day, Swimming Gala, Overseas Study Tour, Adventure Based Activities).
6. Outdoor activities guidelines, legal matters and regulations.
7. Sharing session.
8. Visit and related issues.
9. Field trip.
10. Course summary

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Educational Reform in Chinese Societies
courses.description:
This course employs comparative approaches to analyze educational changes among Chinese societies. An emphasis is placed on the investigation of major reform issues in the Chinese Mainland and Taiwan, China and includes reference to the developmental experiences of Singapore. These issues are also of major interest to educational reformers. The course will include the following topics: (1) the pursuit of quality education; (2) curriculum reform and curriculum integration; (3) reform in teaching and teacher professionalism; (4) decentralization and school-based management; and (5) the expansion of higher education. By drawing insights from the reforms within and across societal contexts of these societies, the course aims to discern implications for the general reform movement as well as school level of daily practices in Hong Kong.

courses.title: Values And Moral Education

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G01

courses.description:
As instituted: “This course aims to help teachers to reflect on their own values and on the ways they teach values, especially moral values, in school. Among other important considerations, students are asked whether teachers should teacher their own values in the classroom, and whether this is indeed inevitable. Taking education as a means aiming at nurturing human qualities for the sake of personal and social well-being, the course examines a range of values such as truth, beauty, goodness and sageness/ saintliness as embodied in ‘whole-person education’. The course holds that education is unavoidably value-laden and that moral values form an important core of the aims of schooling. During the course students will discuss the nature of morality and a number of important approaches to moral education, and then compare these to other types of values education. Students will also be asked to reflect upon how they understand their own personal and professional development in relation to values and moral education and how to enact their various roles in the school.” Topics included please see the lecture outline.

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Teacher Development and Leadership
courses.description:
Teachers are expected to play an increasingly important role in the education reform process. Shifting expectations require teachers to have a firm understanding of how schools operate and how reforms affect their roles both in and outside of the classroom. To effectively reshape their work in line with growing expectations teachers must commit to career long professional development and consider strategies for maximizing their effectiveness, especially in terms of learning and teaching. This course is designed to help teachers to understand and shape their roles in a reform environment. In other words it aims to help teachers to become leaders of their own professionalism. It does this in two ways, first it helps teachers understand life in schools undergoing reform and the effect this can have on their professional life. Topics covered in this area include organizational culture, micropolitics, organizational behaviour and teacher leadership. The second thrust aims to nurture teacher awareness of their own professional growth and how they can maximize the latest opportunities available in this area. Topics covered in this area include models of teacher development, stages of professional development, mentorship and internship, teacher appraisal and teacher professionalism.

courses.title: Ethics and Professional Standards for the Teaching Profession
courses.description:
Professionalism is essential to practices of educators and there must be proper value orientations and solid ethical foundation for the teaching profession. This course covers issues related to law, professional ethics, values and conduct by providing an overview of professional standards for teachers in Hong Kong like T-standard+ and professional code. Case studies are used to examine the rights and responsibilities of teachers vis-a-vis other major stakeholders like students, employers, colleagues, parents/guardians, and to explicate the values and principles teachers can use to make ethical decisions and take ethical actions. Latest issues related to professional development such as education about constitutional order and national security are also addressed.

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Life Education and Pursuit of Meaning
courses.description: Using the tripartite intrapersonal, interpersonal and transcendence competencies framework, this course aims to help students reflect on the meaning of life and examine the importance of physical, psychological and spiritual well-being in life. It will draw on philosophical, socio-cultural, psychological, pedagogical and religious sources, where relevant, to help students reflect on their attitudes towards life through their pursuit of meaning and exploration of ultimate concerns in life education. Students will also learn how to prepare themselves as teachers to help their future pupils cope with related issues in life education.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Overview of life education: HK and international perspectives
2. Intrapersonal competency and self-understanding
3. Mindfulness based education and social emotional well being
4. Physical literacy and its relation to human flourishing
5. Knowing your body through somatic training
6. Interpersonal competency and building relationship
7. Non-violent communication and conflict management
8. Deep listening and compassionate communication
9. Transcendence competency
10. Morality and spirituality

courses.title: Psychology of Learning and Teaching
courses.description:
This course attempts to introduce psychological theories pertinent to the teaching of adolescents in secondary schools. With an emphasis on the application of theories in practice, the following topics are explored: behavioral and cognitive theories of learning, complex cognitive processes, biological basis of learning, motivation and affect, instruction and assessment design and classroom management.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon the completion of this course, students are expected to be able to:

1. Demonstrate an understanding of major psychological theories of learning

2. Apply knowledge of basic cognitive processes (attention and memory) to educational settings

3. Describe higher-order cognition and use metacognitive strategies to improve educational practices

4. Develop knowledge of assessment strategies and use them to improve classroom learning and teaching

5. Acquire basic concepts of classroom management and school discipline

6. Apply effective strategies to foster students’ motivation
courses.course_syllabus:
This course provides a general overview on theories of learning in psychological science and their implications for teaching. The following topics are introduced:

1. Psychological theories of learning

2. Basic cognitive processes: attention and memory

3. Higher-order cognition and metacognition

4. Cognition and instruction

5. Classroom assessments

6. Classroom management and motivation

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Adolescent Development
courses.description:
This course aims to explore the context, nature and dynamics of adolescent development. The roles of family, school, and community in adolescent development will be highlighted. Moreover, teen subcultures will be examined as a key to understanding the psychological needs of adolescents. Current issues of major concern will also be discussed. Emphasis will be placed on students’ theoretical understanding of adolescent development in the social, emotional, cognitive, and moral domains, as well as their application of this knowledge in the school contexts.

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Guidance and Counselling in Secondary Schools
courses.description:
This course intends to provide for secondary school teachers an overview of the basic concepts of school guidance and counselling and their applications in the secondary school setting. Topics include: social and psychological perspectives and the need for school guidance and counselling, basic principles of guidance, goals and objectives of school guidance and counselling, qualification, roles and function of professional counsellor and guidance teacher, basic theories of counselling, individual and group counselling, and other contemporary trends and issues in the local context. In addition, the whole school approach, the therapeutic conditions and the counselling process are also introduced.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Demonstrate an understanding of the basic goals, principles and objectives of school guidance and counselling.

2. Identify various roles and functions of teachers in school guidance and counselling.

3. Gain knowledge of major counselling theories and use them as a guide to understand the social and emotional needs of students.

4. Apply basic counselling skills and interventions to work with students and their families in dealing with students’ socioemotional issues.

5. Identify the conditions and counseling processes that are instrumental to growth and changes

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Understanding and Developing Achievement Tests in Secondary Schools
courses.description:
This course is designed to provide in-service or prospective school teachers with measurement theory and techniques for assessing educational achievements in school.
Topics include
(1) basic concepts and principles of educational measurement and assessment,
(2) procedures for construction and appraisal of objective-type and constructive-type test items,
(3) use of standard achievement tests,
(4) uses of unconventional, informal assessment methods,
(5) methods of interpretation of test scores, and
(6) issues in interpretation and uses of test results.

(Individual course teachers may update the grade descriptors as and whenever necessary. Please refer to the course outline of the respective teachers for details.)

1: Planning classroom tests

1. Taxonomy of instructional objectives

2. Specifying instructional objectives as learning outcomes

3. Test specification and item construction

Topic 2: Constructing objective test items

1. Completion items

2. True-false items

3. Matching items

4. Multiple-choice items

Topic 3: Constructing constructive-response test items: Essay questions

1. Construction of essay questions

2. Approaches to scoring essay response

3. Factors affecting scoring consistency and improving scoring consistency

Topic 4: Assessing high-order thinking, problem solving, and critical thinking skills

1. What are high-order thinking, problem solving, and critical thinking skills?

2. Techniques to assess high-order thinking skills

Topic 5: Constructive-response test items: Performance-based assessments

1. What characterizes performance-based assessments

2. Design ingredients for performance-based assessment

3. Constructing scoring rubrics

4. inter-rater reliability and inter-task reliability of performance-based assessment

Topic 6: Item analysis

1. Item difficulty and item discrimination

2. Item analysis and test reliability/validity

Topic 7: Basic statistics in educational measurement

1. Central tendency

2. Variability

3. Normal distribution

4. Correlational analysis

Topic 8: Validity of assessment results

1. Concept of validity

2. Types of validity evidence

3. Factors affecting validity of assessment results

4. Improving validity of classroom assessments

Topic 9: Reliability of assessment results

1. Concept of reliability

2. Types of reliability

3. Factors affecting reliability of assessment results

4. Improving validity and reliability of classroom assessments

Topic 10: Score interpretations and communications of test results

1. Norm-referenced vs. criterion-referenced interpretation

2. Methods of norm-referenced interpretation of test scores

3. Cautions in interpreting test scores

4. Communicating assessment results and grading

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Sexuality Education in Secondary School
courses.description:
The importance of sexuality education is not merely the communication of facts, but the clarification and establishment of values. Unfortunately, this is exactly the reason why adults, including parents and teachers, often avoid frank discussions about sexuality with young people. In short, adults themselves are trapped in various contradictions and myths about sex in society, which often renders them ineffective in communicating their views and values to youth, providing high-quality sexuality education, and proactively setting effective school policies pertaining to sexuality-related behaviors.

This course discusses various issues related to sexuality, particularly those that are relevant to young people. In-service and pre-service teachers will directly confront and analyze related values, identify common confusions and myths associated with youth sexuality, and examine how their own values might influence the approach they take to providing youth with education related to sexuality. Special emphasis will be given to topics that have direct relevance to adolescents’ sexual health and well-being, but are not typically covered in formal sexuality education curricula. Thus, as opposed to providing teaching methods or ready-to-use teaching materials for classroom demonstration, the primary aims are to raise educators’ awareness of these issues and to help them to proactively clarify their own values in advance of conversations with students. In doing so, they can avoid confusion, misinformation, or unsupportive responses when interacting with youth. By having clear concepts and values regarding sexuality, they can communicate accurate information, provide affirming and supportive guidance to students and advocate for evidence-based school policies in a way that best fits their own instructional contexts.

courses.subject: PGDE
courses.title: Supporting Secondary School Students with Special Educational Needs
courses.description:
This course employs a cross-disciplinary perspective to introduce important issues in supporting students with special educational needs (SEN) in integrated school settings. First, we examine the history, policy and principles of special education and integration in Hong Kong. We then discuss basic principles of identification and intervention for students with SEN with practical skills and examples. Curriculum and instructional issues will be deliberated. In particular, the types of
SEN covered are Specific Learning Difficulties (SpLD), Intellectual Disability (ID), Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (AD/HD), Physical Disability (PD), Visual Impairment (VI), Hearing Impairment (HI), Language Impairment (LI), Non-Chinese Speaking (NCS) and Mental Illness (MI), twice exceptional (i.e. SEN with Giftedness and Talents ) will be covered. Developmental characteristics and needs of these students in secondary school years will be addressed, with a focus on enhancing teachers’ professional capacity in supporting them in the regular classroom and in whole school.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand the history, policy and principles of Integrated Education in Hong Kong.
2. Understand the theories and needs of different types of SEN (including NCS students).
3. Understand the importance of early identification and different evidence-based interventions including three-tier intervention and utilizing resources.
4. Understand the implementation of whole school approach to integrated Education, the roles and responsibilities of different professionals in supporting students SEN and their families.
5. Understand the theories and principles of curriculum development and adaption in different classroom settings for students with SEN.

courses.title: Positive Psychology in Education
courses.description:
This course provides an introduction to the major theoretical orientations for understanding Positive Psychology and Positive Education in a comprehensible way. The objective of this course is to help students understand the core concepts, theories and research of positive psychology, as well as to unpack how positive psychology and positive education can be applied in a secondary school context. To achieve these objectives, students will engage in a variety of activities, including lectures by the instructor, in-class activities, group presentation, group discussions, and individual reflections throughout the course to encourage the exchange and inspiration of ideas.

The course will cover both theoretical and practical knowledge in positive psychology and positive education. For the theoretical part of this course, students will develop knowledge in key theoretical models and forefront research concepts related to positive psychology, with a particular focus on secondary school students from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. An assets-based, positive psychology approach is emphasized in the class with the aim of helping students to “learn from direct experience”. In the practical part of this course, students will acquire the skills and strategies to support the class’s academic success and flourishing. Topics of this course are organized from personal and interpersonal experiences to an institutional lens.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students are expected to be able to:

* Understand the core concepts, theories and research in positive psychology.
* Understand the integration of positive education with students’ motivation, engagement, and achievements.
* Apply knowledge of positive psychology/education to enhance well-being and learning, with the focus on secondary school context.
* Apply the principles, skills, interventions and strategies of positive psychology to foster subjectbased positive education.
* Identify individual positive assets and contextual resources to support secondary school students’ learning and flourishing.
